description: Machine-readable register of corpus papers that are NOT independent evidence of one another (shared participants, shared research programme, review-over-included-trial overlap, commentary/editorial-target pairs, duplicate editions) plus paper-level admission flags (conference abstract slices, commentaries, protocols, non-study documents). Agent 4 consults this at every pair/append decision; G4/G5 reviewers treat it as the standing exclusion set. Every entry was verified against summaries.md / the source PDFs when its beads issue was filed - see source_issue. Append-only: never delete a group, set retired=true with a note instead.

semantics.hard_block: Agent 4 must never emit a conflict, complementary or consensus record that pairs the papers, and must count them as ONE supporter of any verified finding. Applies to relation types: shared_participants, commentary_on, duplicate_edition, letter_on.
semantics.single_source: Both papers may appear in a record, but for consensus independence counting (>=3 independent groups rule) they count as ONE research group, and the record must be labelled as resting on one group where they are the only supporters.
semantics.scope_limited: Non-independent only for the claim families listed in scope; independent for other claims. Agent 4 applies the block when the finding statement matches any scope term; humans decide the rest at G4.
semantics.unconfirmed: Recorded suspicion only. Agent 4 must NOT block on it; it must surface it in the review note so a human decides. Do not assert duplication.

The same Flint editorial (P-786) discusses Kanemoto et al. doi 10.1016/j.inpsyc.2025.100059, already in the corpus as P-428.

Two observational analyses of the SAME DO-HEALTH trial cohort (NCT01745263), same 3-year window, same MoCA<26 MCI definition, four shared authors (Gaengler, Egli, Kressig, Bischoff-Ferrari). Different exposures (haemoglobin vs polypharmacy), so complementary for exposure-specific claims but one cohort for cohort-level claims.
Same Qi Guo lab (Shanghai): shared authors Peipei Han, Xiaoyu Chen, Qi Guo; P-828 cites P-644 as 'our prior research'. Both draw on Shanghai community physical-examination cohorts.

Both systematic reviews include the Morris et al. (2017) exercise trial with identical 34 vs 34 arm sizes; pooled evidence overlaps. Also: reject any record pairing either review with a corpus paper that is one of its own included trials.

P-806 (Saez de Asteasu & Izquierdo, JNHA 2023 mini-review, no data) shares BOTH authors with P-249 (meta-analysis of 16 RCTs). P-806 summarises at least 18 corpus papers (P-249, P-251, P-252, P-256, P-403, P-611, P-613, P-638, P-671, P-672, P-674, P-680, P-683, P-692, P-694, P-698, P-704, P-733). Izquierdo also on P-674 and P-788. P-806 must not be a VF supporter unless an operator confirms it adds independent evidence.

P-819 (Wei et al. 2024 PSG meta-analysis) pools two Shunjie Liu cohorts (Sleep Breath 2020; Sleep Med 2020); Shunjie Liu is first author of P-821 and cites both as his own prior work. P-819 and P-820 share zero included studies and ARE independent.

Shared authors Ujala Sehar and P. Hemachandra Reddy (senior author on both), Texas Tech University HSC; both narrative reviews in Ageing Research Reviews five months apart. P-845 cites P-842 but is a different group (citation link, not non-independence).

Jilin University School of Nursing group. P-833/P-836 share five authors (Yan, Ding, Liu, Chen, Yin); P-838 shares four with both (Qian Liu, Yiwen Ding, Huiru Yin, Li Chen); Yin and Chen are corresponding authors on all three. Included-study rosters of P-833 and P-836 do NOT overlap, so this is authorship/programme dependence, not shared trials.

At least 8 shared included trials by first-author+year (Combourieu Donnezan 2018, Fonte 2019, Hong 2018, Lam 2011, Lam 2015, Law 2019, Nagamatsu 2013, Scherder 2005), verified in both extracts. The P-830 vs P-835 'Tao 2019' key is NOT a shared study (checked false positive).
P-833 shares the Amjad 2019 trial with P-835.

All three draw on the NCGG-SGS programme (Chita / Obu / Tokai City subcohorts, different waves) with shared authors (Makino, Lee, Harada, Katayama, Shimada; Harada, Morikawa, Fujii, Nishijima, Shimada). Participants almost certainly disjoint, so safe for exposure-specific claims, unsafe for claims about NCGG-FAT-defined MCI prevalence or the instrument. P-721 (NCGG Memory Clinic) is independent.

Both sample Rugao City, China (P-258 MPLC survey N=478 MoCA<25; P-824 RuLAS validation cohort N=1788/1823 HDS<21.5). Different surveys, instruments and tasks - probably distinct, but the extracts cannot exclude an overlapping sampling frame. Operator judgment required; do NOT assert duplication.

The taxonomy leaf for P-1029 is labelled '[DUPLICATE-of-P-798] Same paper as P-798 (MarketScan claims-based SuperLearner F1=0.56 ...) kept for numbering/leaf continuity only' while its registry row is live. P-798 is the ISPOR abstract-book slice of the same MarketScan SuperLearner study; P-1029 appears to be the fuller report. Which copy is canonical needs an operator decision before stubbing; until then they are one source.

Same Korean nationwide telephone survey (Gallup, Aug 2022, n=1006, identical metrics 41.3% awareness / 12.0% well informed / WTP-age-SES association). P-629 = WCN 2025 conference abstract (J Neurol Sci 480:124122); P-1415 = full journal article (Dement Neurocogn Disord 24(3):198-207). P-1415 was stubbed to P-629 on 2026-09-05 during batch P-1413..P-1423 after the DOI-based dedup scan missed it (distinct DOIs/venues, same study).

Same Gwangju Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia (GARD) cohort at the Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine, same laboratory and the same oculomotor paradigms (interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade and Go/No-go). Four shared authors: Julius Opwonya (first author on both), Kun Ho Lee, Joong Il Kim and Jaeuk U. Kim (P-966 Front Aging Neurosci 2022;14:871432, DOI 10.3389/fnagi.2022.871432, 249 participants = 79 MCI + 170 age-matched controls; P-1006 Front Neurosci 2023;17:1171417, DOI 10.3389/fnins.2023.1171417, 679 GARD participants recruited October 2019 - December 2020). Neither block prints a participant list, so the exact overlap is not recoverable from the corpus, but the recruitment frame, site, team and paradigms are the same, so they are one source: do not pair them in a conflict, complementary or consensus record and count them as ONE supporter of any eye-movement/MCI finding. Filed on the C-239 operator note, which records that P-1006 was deliberately withheld as a fourth arm of C-239 'because it shares four authors and the GARD cohort with P-966'.

paper_flags._description: Admission flags. conference_abstract: a 1-2 page abstract-book slice, not a full paper - never treat as a full study in counts or synthesis. commentary_editorial: invited commentary/editorial/letter with zero primary data - never a VF supporter on its own. trial_protocol_no_results: planned N only, no observed data. not_a_study: document admitted in error (manual, duplicate stub). fabricated_summary_repaired: block was rewritten from the PDF after a fabrication finding.
